MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A cuboid is 4 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 9 blocks
   B. 24 blocks
   C. 12 blocks
   D. 28 blocks

2. How many cents are in Ksh 25? (1 mark)
   A. 250 cents
   B. 125 cents
   C. 2,500 cents
   D. 25,000 cents

3. How many quarter-litre containers fill 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 2
   C. 4
   D. 3

4. Which way do the hands of a clock move? (1 mark)
   A. Anticlockwise
   B. Clockwise
   C. Sideways
   D. Up and down

5. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 9
   C. 12
   D. 10

6. Estimate 19 × 31 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 500
   B. 700
   C. 600
   D. 6,000

7. Which of these is a multiple of 8? (1 mark)
   A. 74
   B. 72
   C. 73
   D. 71

8. What is 3 L − 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 L
   B. 2 1/2 L
   C. 2 3/4 L
   D. 3 1/4 L

9. Simplify a + a + a. (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. a3
   C. a + 3
   D. 3a

10. What is the next number in the pattern 10,000, 9,000, 8,000, 7,000, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 5,000
   B. 9,000
   C. 6,000
   D. 7,000

11. A customer pays with Ksh 5,000 for goods that cost Ksh 3,350. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1,750
   B. Ksh 8,350
   C. Ksh 1,640
   D. Ksh 1,650

12. Which shape has the same number of rows and columns of unit squares? (1 mark)
   A. A circle
   B. A triangle
   C. A rectangle that is not a square
   D. A square

13. How many minutes are in 12 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 720 minutes
   B. 780 minutes
   C. 1200 minutes
   D. 288 minutes

14. What is 5/6 of 18? (1 mark)
   A. 15
   B. 3
   C. 18
   D. 11

15. In the expression 3m + 2o, what does the letter o stand for if m is a bag of mangoes and 2o is 2 bags of oranges? (1 mark)
   A. Two bags of mangoes
   B. The number 2
   C. One bag of oranges
   D. The total number of bags

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain how you can use addition to check a subtraction. Use 7,865 − 3,542 = 4,323 as an example. (3 marks)

17. A triangle has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Find its perimeter. (2 marks)

18. Wanjiru buys goods worth Ksh 750 and pays with a Ksh 1,000 note. How much change should she get? Check your answer. (3 marks)

19. A jerrycan holds 5 L. Musa pours out 2 1/2 L. How much is left in the jerrycan? (2 marks)

20. Describe how to make a 1/2 L mark on an unmarked bottle using a 1 L container. (3 marks)

21. A garden bed has 9 rows and 4 columns of 1 m squares. Find its area in square metres. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — 24 blocks
   One layer has 4 × 3 = 12 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 12 × 2 = 24 blocks.

2. C — 2,500 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 25 = 25 × 100 = 2,500 cents.

3. C — 4
   Four quarters make one whole, so four 1/4 L containers make 1 L.

4. B — Clockwise
   The hands of a clock move in the direction we call clockwise.

5. D — 10
   Add all the numbers: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

6. C — 600
   19 rounds to 20 and 31 rounds to 30. 20 × 30 = 600.

7. B — 72
   72 = 8 × 9, so 72 is a multiple of 8.

8. C — 2 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 3 L − 1/4 L = 2 3/4 L.

9. D — 3a
   Only like terms can be joined. a + a + a = 3a.

10. C — 6,000
   The rule is subtract 1,000. 7,000 − 1,000 = 6,000.

11. D — Ksh 1,650
   Change = amount paid − cost = 5,000 − 3,350 = Ksh 1,650.

12. D — A square
   A square has equal sides, so its number of rows equals its number of columns.

13. A — 720 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 12 × 60 = 720 minutes.

14. A — 15
   18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 3 × 5 = 15. So 5/6 of 18 is 15.

15. C — One bag of oranges
   The letter o stands for one bag of oranges. The number 2 in front tells us how many bags.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Add the answer to the number that was taken away: 4,323 + 3,542 = 7,865, which is the starting number, so the subtraction is correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying add the answer and the smaller number, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for saying the result matches the starting number.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: 12 cm
   Working / marking points: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12. 1 mark for adding all three sides and 1 mark for the unit.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 250. Check: 750 + 250 = 1,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 1,000 − 750, 1 mark for Ksh 250, 1 mark for the check.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 5 − 2 1/2 = 2 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pour 1 L of water into one bottle. Share it into two identical bottles until the levels match. Mark the water level on one bottle as 1/2 L.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for starting with 1 L, 1 mark for sharing into two equal levels, 1 mark for marking 1/2 L.

21. (2 marks)
   Answer: 36 square metres
   Working / marking points: 9 × 4 = 36. 1 mark for the multiplication and 1 mark for the unit.
